Change c0316. Location: 1818 Vol. II, Ch. VIII; 1831 Ch. XVI.

Context before (unchanged): "'Frankenstein! you belong then to my enemy—to him towards whom I have sworn eternal revenge; you shall be my first victim.'

1818 text: "The child still struggled, and loaded me with epithets which carried despair to my heart: I grasped his throat to silence him, and in a moment he lay dead at my feet. "I gazed on my victim, and my heart swelled with exultation and hellish triumph: clapping my hands, I exclaimed, 'I, too, can create desolation; my enemy is not impregnable; this death will carry despair to him, and a thousand other miseries shall torment and destroy him.'

1831 text: "The child still struggled, and loaded me with epithets which carried despair to my heart; I grasped his throat to silence him, and in a moment he lay dead at my feet. "I gazed on my victim, and my heart swelled with exultation and hellish triumph: clapping my hands, I exclaimed, 'I, too, can create desolation; my enemy is not invulnerable; this death will carry despair to him, and a thousand other miseries shall torment and destroy him.'

" I gazed on my victim, and my heart swelled with exultation and hellish triumph: clapping my hands, I exclaimed, 'I, too, can create desolation; my enemy is not [-impregnable-] {+invulnerable+} ; this death will carry despair to him, and a thousand other miseries shall torment and destroy him. '

Context after (unchanged): "As I fixed my eyes on the child, I saw something glittering on his breast.

result.rationale: Replaces 'impregnable' with 'invulnerable' (and colon with semicolon in the sentence before); same meaning of the creature's enemy being unassailable. Stylistic diction shift, with the 'invulnerable' choice slightly more physical and ironic.
